methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion, a Series G robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date, is evaluated against a comp universe of nine sector peers: one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Of the available triangulation methods, only stage-progression proves applicable. The peer-median approach cannot be executed due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while eight same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier yields fewer than three datapoints required for statistical reliability. The stage-progression method applies a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement to the $150M total-raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $188M.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $159M (low) to $216M (median $188M), centered on the single applicable method. The primary uncertainty stems from limited peer comparability; a more robust conclusion would require either additional same-stage robotics comparables or access to recent secondary transaction data for Distalmotion itself. The wide range ($57M spread) reflects methodological constraint rather than fundamental disagreement among approaches. Given the single-method foundation, sensitivity to the 1.25x multiplier assumption should be monitored in any follow-on analysis.
